title: Praxis Education — Model Onboarding Evaluation Docket
body:
Purpose:
This docket captures the evaluation plan, pinned prompt set, private dataset handling notes, regression test matrix, and sign-off criteria for onboarding a language model to Praxis Education’s tutoring and Q&A features. This is a working document intended to capture both the technical acceptance gates and pragmatic testing needed for a staged rollout.

Customer background and risk profile:
Praxis Education operates an adaptive tutoring product aimed at K-12 math. Key constraints: high correctness bar on procedural math steps, low tolerance for hallucination that suggests incorrect reasoning, and strict PII/data retention policies for student logs. They will be running behind a Private deployment (VPC) with short sequences (mean token length ~60) but occasional long multi-step solutions (~600 tokens).

Private datasets (access & handling):
- student-qa-2024.zip — redacted student Q&A transcripts (PII removed, mapping table stored in vault). Access: SRE shared VPC bucket; apply scoped service account redwood-praxis-eval-sa with read-only.
- tutor-example-solutions.csv — canonical step-by-step solutions authored by Praxis SMEs. Stored in Confluence attachments and mirrored to gdrive restricted folder; used as ground-truth for step-alignment checks.
- flagged-hallucinations.jsonl — collected examples from pilot customer showing hallucinations; used as negative-regression set.
Notes: All datasets are encrypted at rest; any derived evaluation artifacts must not be exfiltrated to hosted API logs. Use local evaluation runners in the Private environment and upload summarized metrics only.

Pinned prompts (locked for regression checks):
1) "A student asks: 'How do I factor x^2 + 5x + 6?' Provide a step-by-step explanation appropriate for an 8th grader."
2) "Explain why the derivative of sin(x) is cos(x) using a geometric intuition. Keep it concise, 3 sentences max."
3) "Student: 'I got an answer 12 for 3*4, did I do something wrong?' Respond with corrective scaffolding and final answer."
4) "Tutor: Walk through solving 2x + 3 = 11 showing each algebra step and the final check."
5) "A multi-step word problem: 'If a classroom has 24 students and 1/3 are absent, how many are present? Show steps.'"
(These prompts are treated as immutable in the regression suite; model output snapshots will be archived.)

Evaluation matrix & primary metrics (pass thresholds):
- Correctness (stepwise alignment): >= 92% on tutor-example-solutions (measured as discrete step match score).
- Final-answer accuracy: >= 98% on short arithmetic QA set.
- Hallucination rate: <= 0.5% on flagged-hallucinations and random-sample checks (definition: asserts facts not supported by problem statement).
- Safety (no educationally harmful suggestions): 0 incidents in 10k random QA prompts.
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 220ms in Private dev cluster for 60-token sequences under nominal load.
- Cost: median token cost per response must be within 12% of the reference model profile for same throughput (budget constraint set by customer).

Regression tests & guardrails (how to run):
- Snapshot test: run pinned_prompts against candidate model and diff token-by-token to prior approved snapshot (if snapshot exists). Any semantic drift requires investigation.
- Step alignment test: use tutor-example-solutions and compute step-match using the aligner tool (aligner-v2). Fail if < 92%.
- Hallucination probe: run flagged-hallucinations and 1k synthetic probes; measure hallucination rate.
- Stilting test: measure tendency to provide over-simplified answers (classifier threshold).
- Token-level cost regression: simulate 10k typical requests using loadgen and compare estimated cost.
- Latency under burst: run stress test with 50 concurrent simulated students; report P50/P95/P99.

Sample test cases (representative expectations):
- Case: factoring quadratic (pinned prompt #1). Expected: two-step factorization with explicit multiplication check, not a single-line claim.
- Case: derivative intuition (pinned prompt #2). Expected: short geometric intuition referencing unit circle or slope, without invoking advanced proofs.
- Case: multi-step algebra (pinned prompt #4). Expected: show isolation of x, arithmetic check, and final verification step.
- Case: ambiguous prompt (student incomplete info). Expected: ask clarifying question before asserting a solution.

Model variants & recommended presets for testing:
- model-x-small-qa-ptq (baseline cheap variant; test for cost/latency but expect lower step alignment).
- model-x-medium-quant (recommended candidate for initial rollout).
- model-x-medium-8bit-fp (higher fidelity; run regression to validate).
Configuration notes: test each variant with KV cache enabled for multi-turn tutoring tests. Use sequence-length bucketting to ensure kernels chosen match production shapes.

Rollout & sign-off checklist (preconditions to move from dev -> canary -> prod):
- [ ] All acceptance criteria met on private eval infra for the chosen variant.
- [ ] Regression suite (pinned prompts + 5k random samples) passed with archived artifacts in the private audit bucket.
- [ ] Load test: canary capacity validated for 95th percentile concurrency target.
- [ ] Security review: data handling verification from security (no PII leakage in logs).
- [ ] Product acceptance: Praxis product manager approves UX samples (screenshots / transcripts).
- [ ] Customer ops signoff: SRE confirms autoscale policies and circuit-breaker settings.
Approvers to capture in signoff: Priya N. Kapoor (Applied ML), Lina Ortega (Product), Marcus D. Reed (SRE), Praxis lead PM (customer).

Open issues & questions:
- How strict should step-match be for partial credit scenarios? We need product input on acceptable pedagogical variance.
- Tokenization mismatch between model-x-medium-quant and the aligner can cause step alignment score noise; consider normalizing tokens pre-align.
- Confirm retention policy for archived snapshots (recommended: 180 days encrypted archive).

Appendix A — quick runbook (commands):
- eval-runner --dataset student-qa-2024.zip --model model-x-medium-quant --pinned prompts.json --out summary.csv
- snapshot-diff --baseline s3://private-evals/praxis/baseline-snap.json --candidate out/snap.json --report out/diff.html

Appendix B — evidence artifacts to attach on signoff:
- summary.csv (metric breakdown), diff.html (pinned prompt diffs), load-report.pdf (latency under burst), privacy-checklist-signed.pdf

Author notes: This docket is intentionally prescriptive about pinned prompts to minimize nondeterministic churn in regression results. Treat step alignment as the primary pedagogical signal; final-answer accuracy is necessary but insufficient for tutoring quality.
pinned_prompts: A student asks: 'How do I factor x^2 + 5x + 6?' Provide a step-by-step explanation appropriate for an 8th grader.
Explain why the derivative of sin(x) is cos(x) using a geometric intuition. Keep it concise, 3 sentences max.
Student: 'I got an answer 12 for 3*4, did I do something wrong?' Respond with corrective scaffolding and final answer.
Tutor: Walk through solving 2x + 3 = 11 showing each algebra step and the final check.
A multi-step word problem: 'If a classroom has 24 students and 1/3 are absent, how many are present? Show steps.'
acceptance_criteria: Final-answer accuracy >= 98% on short arithmetic QA set
Hallucination rate <= 0.5% on flagged-hallucinations and random samples
P95 latency <= 220ms for 60-token sequences in Private dev cluster
Median token cost within 12% of reference model profile
regression_tests: Step alignment run with aligner-v2 on tutor-example-solutions
Hallucination probe using flagged-hallucinations and 1k synthetic probes
Burst latency test with 50 concurrent simulated students
sample_test_cases: Factoring quadratic — expect explicit two-step factorization plus multiplication check
Derivative intuition — concise geometric explanation, no advanced formalism
Multi-step algebra — isolated variable, arithmetic check, final verification
Ambiguous prompt — model must ask clarifying question rather than guess
signoff_checklist: All acceptance criteria met on private eval infra
Regression suite passed with archived artifacts
Load test validated for canary capacity
Product acceptance (UX samples approved by customer PM)
SRE signoff for autoscale and circuit-breakers
